questions.question_english:
Consider the following components of school infrastructure:
I. Ramps with handrails
II. Accessible toilets
III. Tactile pathways
Which of the components given above are essential requirements for a barrier-free school environment according to accessibility norms?
options_english: I and II only
II and III only
I and III only
I, II and III
questions.explanation_english: Creating an inclusive, barrier-free school environment under the RPwD Act, 2016 (Sections 16 & 40) and the Harmonised Guidelines requires all three components: (I) Ramps with continuous double-tier handrails (at heights of 750 mm and 900 mm) and a standard 1:12 gradient ensure smooth, independent vertical mobility for students using wheelchairs, crutches, or walkers; (II) Accessible unisex toilets with wide sliding or outward-swinging doors, grab bars, low-height washbasins, and emergency call buttons ensure privacy, safety, and hygiene; (III) Tactile ground indicators (guiding and warning pavers) enable visually impaired students to orient themselves, locate entrances, and navigate school corridors safely without risk of collision or falls. Hence, I, II, and III are all essential requirements.
questions.explanation_hindi: दिव्यांगजन अधिकार अधिनियम, 2016 की धारा 16 व 40 तथा समेकित दिशा-निर्देशों (Harmonised Guidelines) के अनुसार, बाधा-मुक्त विद्यालय परिवेश के निर्माण हेतु तीनों घटक अनिवार्य हैं: (I) मानक 1:12 ढलान और दोनों तरफ 750 मिमी व 900 मिमी पर दोहरी रेलिंग वाले रैंप व्हीलचेयर और बैसाखी का उपयोग करने वाले विद्यार्थियों के निर्बाध आवागमन को सुनिश्चित करते हैं; (II) चौड़े दरवाजों, ग्रैब बार्स और उपयुक्त ऊंचाई वाले सेनेटरी फिटिंग्स से युक्त सुगम शौचालय शारीरिक दिव्यांग विद्यार्थियों की स्वच्छता व गरिमा सुनिश्चित करते हैं; तथा (III) स्पर्शनीय पाथवे (Tactile pathways/pavers) दृष्टिबाधित विद्यार्थियों को विद्यालय परिसर, गलियारों और सीढ़ियों पर सुरक्षित व स्वतंत्र रूप से आवागमन करने में सहायता करते हैं। अतः I, II और III तीनों अनिवार्य हैं।

key_facts: Printed answer key: (d) I, II and III

questions.explanation_english:
Section 31(1) of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016 contains a non-obstante clause that explicitly expands upon the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009. It stipulates:
'Notwithstanding anything contained in the Rights of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009, every child with benchmark disability between the age of six to eighteen years shall have the right to free education in a neighbourhood school, or in a special school, of his choice.'

While the RTE Act guarantees free education to general children up to the age of 14 years (elementary education from classes 1 to 8), Section 31 of the RPwD Act deliberately extends this entitlement up to the age of 18 years (covering secondary and senior secondary schooling). This statutory recognition accommodates potential late enrollment, medical interruptions, and the extended learning pace of children with disabilities.
questions.explanation_hindi:
दिव्यांगजन अधिकार अधिनियम (RPwD Act), 2016 की धारा 31(1) में एक विशिष्ट प्रावधान है जो निःशुल्क और अनिवार्य बाल शिक्षा का अधिकार (RTE) अधिनियम, 2009 के प्रावधानों का विस्तार करता है। धारा 31(1) के अनुसार:
'निःशुल्क और अनिवार्य बाल शिक्षा का अधिकार अधिनियम, 2009 में किसी बात के होते हुए भी, छह से अठारह वर्ष की आयु के बीच बेंचमार्क दिव्यांगता वाले प्रत्येक बच्चे को अपनी पसंद के पड़ोस के विद्यालय या किसी विशेष विद्यालय में निःशुल्क शिक्षा प्राप्त करने का अधिकार होगा।'

सामान्य बच्चों के लिए आरटीई अधिनियम, 2009 के तहत निःशुल्क शिक्षा 6 से 14 वर्ष (कक्षा 8 तक) के लिए सुनिश्चित है, जबकि RPwD अधिनियम, 2016 की धारा 31 इस विधिक अधिकार को 18 वर्ष (कक्षा 12/उच्च माध्यमिक स्तर) तक बढ़ाती है ताकि दिव्यांग बच्चों को उनकी विशिष्ट आवश्यकताओं और उपचार संबंधी विलंब के बावजूद माध्यमिक स्तर तक पूर्णतः निःशुल्क शिक्षा मिल सके।

questions.explanation_english:
Form 26AS is the consolidated Annual Tax Statement generated by the Income Tax Department under Section 203AA read with Rule 31AB for every PAN holder.

Form 26AS provides a comprehensive record of:
1. Tax Deducted at Source (TDS) by employers (salaries) and other deductors (contractors, bank interest, professional fees).
2. Tax Collected at Source (TCS) by sellers.
3. Advance tax and self-assessment tax paid directly by the taxpayer.
4. Details of income tax refunds received during the financial year.
5. Specified Financial Transactions (SFT) reported by banks and financial institutions.

Other forms:
- Form 12BA: Statement showing perquisites and other fringe benefits provided to an employee.
- Form 16B: TDS certificate for tax deducted under Section 194-IA on the purchase of immovable property.
- Form 15G: Self-declaration form to claim exemption from TDS on interest income by individuals below 60 years.
questions.explanation_hindi:
फॉर्म 26AS प्रत्येक पैन धारक के लिए आयकर अधिनियम की धारा 203AA और नियम 31AB के तहत आयकर विभाग द्वारा तैयार किया जाने वाला समेकित वार्षिक कर विवरण (Annual Tax Statement) है।

फॉर्म 26AS में निम्नलिखित का व्यापक रिकॉर्ड होता है:
1. नियोक्ताओं (वेतन) तथा अन्य कटौतीकर्ताओं (ठेकेदारों, बैंक ब्याज, व्यावसायिक शुल्क आदि) द्वारा काटा गया स्रोत पर कर (TDS)।
2. विक्रेताओं द्वारा स्रोत पर संगृहीत कर (TCS)।
3. करदाता द्वारा सीधे जमा किया गया अग्रिम कर (Advance Tax) और स्व-निर्धारण कर (Self-Assessment Tax)।
4. वित्तीय वर्ष के दौरान प्राप्त आयकर रिफंड का विवरण।
5. बैंकों और वित्तीय संस्थानों द्वारा रिपोर्ट किए गए निर्दिष्ट वित्तीय लेनदेन (SFT)।

questions.question_english:
Consider the following Constitutional Amendments:
I. 77th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1995
II. 81st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2000
III. 85th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2001

Which of the following aspects of affirmative action in public employment under Article 16 are addressed by these amendments collectively?
options_english: Economic reservation, upper-caste quotas, and private school admission mandates
Promotion reservation, the carry-forward rule for backlog vacancies, and consequential seniority
Mandating 27% reservation for OBC candidates across all central services and PSUs
Abolishing the creamy layer exclusion principle for backward classes in public employment
questions.explanation_english:
The 77th, 81st, and 85th Constitutional Amendments collectively fortified and restructured affirmative action in public employment under Article 16 of the Constitution of India:

1. 77th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1995: Inserted clause (4A) into Article 16 to enable the State to provide reservation in matters of promotion for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, overriding the prohibition on promotional reservation laid down in Indra Sawhney (1992).

2. 81st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2000: Inserted clause (4B) into Article 16 to protect the 'carry forward' rule. It provided that unfilled backlog vacancies of a year reserved under clause (4) or (4A) constitute a distinct class that is not subject to the 50% reservation ceiling in succeeding years.

3. 85th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2001: Amended Article 16(4A) with retrospective effect from 17 June 1995 to incorporate the words 'with consequential seniority' for SC and ST employees promoted through reservation rosters, effectively overcoming the judicial 'catch-up rule'.

Together, these three amendments specifically cover: Promotion reservation, the carry-forward rule for backlog vacancies, and consequential seniority.

1. 77वां संविधान संशोधन अधिनियम, 1995: इसने अनुच्छेद 16 में खंड (4A) जोड़ा, जिससे राज्य को इंद्रा साहनी (1992) के निर्णय के प्रभाव को समाप्त करते हुए अनुसूचित जातियों और अनुसूचित जनजातियों के लिए पदोन्नति में आरक्षण प्रदान करने की शक्ति मिली।

2. 81वां संविधान संशोधन अधिनियम, 2000: इसने अनुच्छेद 16 में खंड (4B) जोड़ा, जिससे 'कैरी-फॉरवर्ड' (आगे ले जाने का) नियम सुरक्षित हुआ। इसके अनुसार बैकलॉग रिक्तियों को एक अलग वर्ग माना जाता है और उन पर अगले वर्षों में 50% की आरक्षण सीमा लागू नहीं होती।

3. 85वां संविधान संशोधन अधिनियम, 2001: इसने 17 जून 1995 से भूतलक्षी प्रभाव से अनुच्छेद 16(4A) में संशोधन कर 'परिणामी वरिष्ठता सहित' (with consequential seniority) शब्दावली जोड़ी, जिससे सर्वोच्च न्यायालय द्वारा प्रतिपादित 'कैच-अप नियम' का प्रभाव समाप्त हो गया।

questions.question_english: The Permanent Account Number (PAN) issued by the Income Tax Department under Section 139A of the Income Tax Act is a unique alphanumeric identifier. How many characters does a standard PAN contain?
questions.explanation_english:
A Permanent Account Number (PAN) issued under Section 139A of the Income Tax Act, 1961 is a 10-character alphanumeric code structured as follows:
- Characters 1 to 3: Alphabetic series running from AAA to ZZZ.
- Character 4: Status of the PAN holder (e.g., 'P' for Individual/Person, 'C' for Company, 'F' for Firm, 'T' for Trust, 'G' for Government).
- Character 5: First character of the surname/last name of an individual, or first character of the entity's registered name.
- Characters 6 to 9: Sequential four-digit numerical sequence running from 0001 to 9999.
- Character 10: Alphabetic check digit.
Thus, every PAN consists of exactly 10 characters.

आयकर अधिनियम, 1961 की धारा 139A के अंतर्गत जारी स्थायी खाता संख्या (PAN) 10-वर्णों (10-digit alphanumeric) का एक विशिष्ट कोड होता है। इसकी संरचना निम्न प्रकार होती है:
- पहले 3 वर्ण: AAA से ZZZ तक वर्णमाला की श्रृंखला।
- चौथा वर्ण: पैन धारक का दर्जा/प्रस्थिति (जैसे व्यष्टि/व्यक्ति के लिए 'P', कंपनी के लिए 'C', ट्रस्ट के लिए 'T', फर्म के लिए 'F', सरकार के लिए 'G')।

- अगले 4 वर्ण (6 से 9): 0001 से 9999 तक अनुक्रमिक चार अंक।
- 10वाँ वर्ण: एक वर्णमाला चेक डिजिट (alphabetic check digit)।

questions.explanation_english: Prior to 2005, Article 15(4) enabled reservations and special provisions primarily in government-run and state-aided educational institutions. In landmark decisions like T.M.A. Pai Foundation (2002) and P.A. Inamdar v. State of Maharashtra (2005), the Supreme Court ruled that the State could not impose reservation quotas on private unaided educational institutions, holding that such restrictions violated the fundamental right to carry on an occupation under Article 19(1)(g). To bridge this critical constitutional gap and ensure that private unaided professional colleges and schools share the burden of affirmative action, Parliament enacted the 93rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2005, inserting Article 15(5). This clause specifically empowered the State to mandate reservations in educational institutions, including private unaided institutions, other than minority educational institutions.

questions.explanation_english: Under Section 51 of the Central Goods and Services Tax (CGST) Act, 2017, government departments, local authorities, and specified governmental agencies are designated as deductors of Tax Deducted at Source (TDS) under GST. questions.question_english: What is the statutory minimum monetary compensation prescribed under the POSH Act, 2013 that must be awarded to an aggrieved woman?
options_english: A fixed statutory minimum of ₹50,000 payable by the employer
A fixed statutory minimum of ₹1,00,000 payable by the employer
An amount fixed at exactly three months of the respondent's gross salary
There is no fixed minimum amount; it is determined by the Internal Committee based on statutory factors
questions.explanation_english: The POSH Act, 2013 does not prescribe any flat or statutory minimum numerical sum as compensation. Instead, under Section 15 of the Act, the Internal Committee (or Local Committee) determines the compensation to be paid by the respondent to the aggrieved woman on a case-by-case basis. The committee evaluates specific parameters outlined in Section 15, including: (a) mental trauma, pain, suffering, and emotional distress caused to the woman; (b) loss in career opportunity due to the harassment; (c) medical expenses incurred for physical or psychiatric treatment; (d) the income and financial status of the respondent; and (e) the feasibility of such payment in lump sum or installments. Therefore, compensation is determined purely on merits and statutory criteria rather than any predefined floor amount.

options_english: 2 copies

6 copies
8 copies
questions.explanation_english:
Under Rule 6(1) of the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Rules, 2013:
'For the purpose of sub-section (2) of section 9, a complainant shall submit to the Complaints Committee, six copies of the complaint along with supporting documents and the names and addresses of the witnesses.'

Procedural and Administrative Rationale:
1. Service of Notice on Respondent: Under Rule 7(1), the committee must forward one complete copy of the complaint with all attachments to the respondent within seven working days of receipt.
2. Quorum and Committee Dossiers: The ICC consists of a Presiding Officer, at least two employee members, and one external member (minimum 4 members). Individual copies ensure each member has access to the full complaint docket for independent scrutiny and questioning.
3. Official Dossier: One copy remains in the permanent sealed archive of the committee.

Therefore, Rule 6 mandates submission of exactly 6 copies (Option C).
questions.explanation_hindi:
कार्यस्थल पर महिलाओं का लैंगिक उत्पीड़न (निवारण, प्रतिषेध एवं प्रतितोष) नियम, 2013 के नियम 6(1) के अंतर्गत:
'धारा 9 की उपधारा (2) के प्रयोजनार्थ, शिकायतकर्ता को शिकायत समिति के समक्ष समर्थक दस्तावेजों तथा गवाहों के नाम व पते के साथ शिकायत की 6 प्रतियां प्रस्तुत करनी होंगी।'

प्रशासनिक व प्रक्रियात्मक कारण:
1. प्रत्यर्थी को तामील: नियम 7(1) के अनुसार, शिकायत प्राप्त होने के 7 कार्यदिवसों के भीतर समिति को एक प्रति सभी संलग्न दस्तावेजों सहित प्रत्यर्थी (आरोपी) को जवाब हेतु भेजनी होती है।
2. समिति सदस्यों में वितरण: शेष प्रतियां आंतरिक समिति के सदस्यों (पीठासीन अधिकारी, दो विभागीय सदस्य और एक बाहरी सदस्य - न्यूनतम 4 सदस्य) को अवलोकन व साक्ष्य परीक्षण हेतु प्रदान की जाती हैं।
3. कार्यालय अभिलेख: एक प्रति समिति की आधिकारिक एवं गोपनीय पत्रावली (डॉक्युमेंट फाइल) में सुरक्षित रखी जाती है।

अतः विधिक नियमों के अनुसार अनिवार्य प्रतियों की संख्या 6 है (विकल्प C)।

questions.question_english: Are Railway Servants governed by the CCS (CCA) Rules, 1965?

questions.explanation_english: No, because they are governed by the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules. questions.question_english: What is the statutory rate of interest charged under Section 201(1A) of the Income Tax Act, 1961 for delayed deposit of TDS (i.e., where tax has been deducted but not paid to the government account)?

questions.explanation_english:
Under Section 201(1A) of the Income Tax Act, 1961, if a deductor fails to deduct or pay TDS, mandatory simple interest is levied as follows:

1. For failure/delay in deducting tax: Simple interest at 1.0% per month or part of a month, from the date on which tax was deductible to the date on which tax is actually deducted.
2. For failure/delay in depositing tax after deduction: Simple interest at 1.5% per month or part of a month, from the date on which tax was deducted to the date on which such tax is actually paid/deposited into the government treasury.

Since this question specifically asks about delayed deposit (tax deducted but not deposited), the applicable rate is 1.5% per month or part of a month. This interest cannot be waived and must be paid before filing the quarterly return.

Income from House Property
Income from Capital Gains
questions.explanation_english:
Under Section 14 of the Income Tax Act, 1961, all income for the purposes of charge of income-tax and computation of total income is classified under exactly five statutory heads of income:
1. Salaries (Sections 15–17)
2. Income from house property (Sections 22–27)
3. Profits and gains of business or profession (Sections 28–44DB)
4. Capital gains (Sections 45–55A)
5. Income from other sources (Sections 56–59).
There is no statutory head called 'Income from Bank Deposits'. Interest earned from savings accounts, fixed deposits, or recurring deposits in banks is assessed under the residual head 'Income from Other Sources' (Section 56).
questions.explanation_hindi:
आयकर अधिनियम, 1961 की धारा 14 के अनुसार कुल आय की गणना के लिए आय को केवल पाँच वैधानिक शीर्षों (Heads of Income) में वर्गीकृत किया गया है:
1. वेतन से आय
2. गृह संपत्ति से आय
3. व्यवसाय या पेशे के लाभ एवं अभिलाभ
4. पूंजीगत अभिलाभ
5. अन्य स्रोतों से आय।
'बैंक जमा से आय' कोई स्वतंत्र शीर्ष नहीं है; बैंक सावधि जमा (FD) या बचत खाते से प्राप्त ब्याज धारा 56 के अंतर्गत 'अन्य स्रोतों से आय' शीर्ष के अधीन कर-योग्य होता है।
